newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco ports cash turnover up, cargo falls.
newsitem.headline: Morocco ports cash turnover up, cargo falls.

text.p: Morocco's Ports' Operating Office said turnover in 1996 totalled 1.5 billion dirhams ($166 million), a rise of 1.5 percent over the previous year despite a fall in cargo traffic.
The official Moroccan news agency MAP said on Sunday that ports office director general Mohamed Halab reported that traffic reached 42.6 million tonnes last year compared with 44 million in 1995.
The 3.1 percent fall was due to a drop in hydrocarbon, sulphor and phosphoric acid tonnages.
Halab told a ports office meeting that Casablanca, where a new container terminal had been brought into operation, remained the country's premier port, handling 37.6 percent of global traffic.
Containers had also been handled for the first time last year in Nador port.
Morocco's ports had handled a total of 221,000 containers, an increase of 2.4 percent over 1995.
